content:
Maria K: Hey team, spotted something weird in the nightly evals. Looks like the same schedule job ran twice between 02:00 and 02:05 UTC.
Ajay P: Huh, any logs/ids?
Maria K: Pasting a snippet from the GH Actions run list:
```
2026-03-18T02:00:01Z  workflow: nightly-evals  run_id: 987654321
2026-03-18T02:01:12Z  workflow: nightly-evals  run_id: 987654322
```
Sophie L: Two run_ids for the same cron window — did we have both `schedule` and a `workflow_dispatch` triggered by some bot? Or tz confusion?
Ben R: Workflow file attached earlier had `cron: '0 18 * * *'` which we wrote thinking PST. GH Actions uses UTC so that becomes 18:00 UTC not 18:00 PST — but double-run sounds different.
Maria K: Also saw PR gating slowdowns yesterday — runners were saturated while both runs executed. Eval runner queue got backlogged and some quant smoke tests hit OOM.
eval-bot: nightly-eval: started run 987654321 on runner self-hosted-ml-1
eval-bot: nightly-eval: started run 987654322 on runner self-hosted-ml-2
eval-bot: nightly-eval: run 987654321 finished (ok: 58, fail: 1 - models/quant-A OOM)
eval-bot: nightly-eval: run 987654322 finished (ok: 57, fail: 2 - models/quant-A OOM, models/quant-B mismatch)
Ajay P: If two different runners picked up the same scheduled event we might have duplicate scheduling from two workflows — check for duplicate workflow files or a cron in a parent pipeline.
Ben R: I pulled the repo: we have `.github/workflows/nightly-evals.yml` and also a legacy `.github/workflows/nightly-evals-legacy.yml` that still has the same cron. Looks like both are active.
Sophie L: That explains it. Legacy file should have been archived but GH ignored the branch filter. Quick fix: add `concurrency` to both workflows and set `cancel-in-progress: true` so duplicates cancel.
Ben R: Proposed patch snippet:
```
concurrency:
  group: nightly-evals-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```
Sophie L: Also add `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` guard on the job that does heavy runner usage so `workflow_dispatch` (manual runs) don't overlap with schedule, and add a `tags: [nightly]` label so queueing favors dedicated machines.
Maria K: Can we also add a quick idempotency check in the eval runner: if another run with the same commit + job-name is active, skip? That'd avoid duplicate side effects.
Ajay P: I'll open a PR with three things: remove legacy workflow (or at least disable cron), add concurrency cancel-in-progress, add the `if: github.event_name == 'schedule'` guard for heavy jobs. Test plan: create a temporary cron at 5 minutes in the future on a branch and watch for single run.
Ben R: Also propose adding small change to buildkite/runner labels so PR gating uses a different pool than nightly to avoid interference.
Maria K: Sounds good. Assigning to @Ajay P. Can you include a short smoke test that runs quant-A with tiny batch to reproduce OOM quickly?
Ajay P: Yep. Will do. I'll also add a log snippet capture to eval-bot so next time we have clearer evidence (runner id + concurrency token).
infra-bot: branch created: ajay/gha-nightly-concurrency-patch (links: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/432)
Maria K: Thanks — will monitor next 48h and flag if we still see dupes. :thumbsup:
